papers.title: Supplementary Video S1: Doing More with Less – Complex Manipulation with a Contact-Adaptive Robotic Hand
papers.summary: This supplementary video accompanies the manuscript "Doing More with Less: Complex Manipulation with a Contact-Adaptive Robotic Hand" by Hyung Gon Shin and Sanghoon Jung. The video presents experimental demonstrations of a five-fingered anthropomorphic robotic hand incorporating a contact-adaptive split-stage gear–spring mechanism. The robotic hands are controlled through motion gloves and a branch-shadowing interface, allowing the operator to provide arm movements, bimanual coordination, perception, and decision-making. papers.title: Evaluating the Ecological Validity and Mechanism of a Generative Model-Based Decomposition of Affective Variability
papers.summary: Affective variability is a pervasive phenomenon with important implications for cognition, behavior, and well-being. Yet the broad concept of variability may conflate distinct processes, such as transient fluctuations versus more sustained shifts. Computational approaches like reinforcement learning (RL) offer a mechanistic framework for these processes, but they are often studied in artificial settings, raising questions about ecological validity. papers.title: Robotic surgery in gastrointestinal emergency settings: A systematic review
papers.summary: BACKGROUND Robotic-assisted surgery has become an established component of elective minimally invasive surgery, yet its role in emergency gastrointestinal surgery remains uncertain. Emergency procedures pose unique challenges, including time-critical decision-making, complex anatomy, and limited opportunities for extensive preoperative planning. AIM To evaluate the current evidence regarding the feasibility, safety, and clinical outcomes of robotic surgery in the emergency gastrointestinal setting. METHODS A systematic literature search of PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library was performed

papers.title: A robotic neck exoskeleton for children with poor head control: a feasibility study
papers.summary: The ability to properly orient the head is essential for learning motor and cognitive skills in child development. Children with severe motor disabilities often struggle to hold their head upright and move it in a controlled manner. Existing solutions, such as passive head equipment and physical therapy, are limited and insufficient. We recently developed a robotic neck exoskeleton to support the head and control its three-dimensional movements. papers.title: Digital-physical testbed for ship autonomy studies in the Marine Cybernetics Laboratory basin
papers.summary: The algorithms developed for Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS) are often challenging to test on actual vessels due to high operational costs and safety considerations. Simulations offer a cost-effective alternative and eliminate risks, but they may not accurately represent real-world dynamics for the given tasks. Utilizing small-scale model ships and robotic vessels in conjunction with a laboratory basin provides an accessible testing environment for the early stages of validation processes. papers.title: Governing the next generation: a framework for the safe and equitable deployment of artificial intelligence, robotics, and immersive technologies in ophthalmology
papers.summary: Objective A new generation of technologies – artificial intelligence (AI), AI-guided surgical robotics, and immersive systems including virtual and augmented reality – are transforming ophthalmic practice across diagnoses, surgery, training, and patient engagement. Each domain has generated compelling clinical evidence; each has also exposed governance gaps – that, if unaddressed, risk entrenching inequalities, undermining patient safety, and erode clinical trust. papers.title: Practice Is Not Free: Measuring the Embodied Cost of Reset-Free Robot Practice
papers.summary: When a robot practices without human resets, every attempt still costs wall-clock time, actuator wear, and sometimes a person's attention, yet the schedulers that decide what to practice next treat attempts as free. We present an open, low-cost testbed for measuring these costs: a self-built SO-101 arm runs two demonstration-trained ACT policies that reset each other, with a vision-based success detector and a ledger that records the time, joint travel, and human interventions of every attempt. papers.title: Surface Microstructure Engineering of Carbon Black/Ecoflex Nanocomposite for Enhanced Piezoresistive Sensors Performance
papers.summary: Flexible strain sensors based on piezoresistive mechanism have gained considerable interest in wearable devices, soft robotic system and electronic skin due to its advantages such as flexible and capability to detect mechanical deformation through electrical signal variation. Despite recent advances, developing sensors with reliable sensitivity, simple fabrication, and cost-effective processing remains a significant challenge. papers.title: Optimization method for spatial robot arm locking-unit layout based on plant root adaptive growth patterns
papers.summary: Purpose To address the optimization problem of spatial robotic arm locking-unit layout, this study proposes a collaborative optimization method based on the adaptive growth patterns of plant roots. papers.title: Contextual Bandits and Optimistically Universal Learning
papers.summary: We consider the contextual bandit problem in general action and context spaces. This generalizes the standard multiarmed bandit to the case where side information is available—for example, patients’ records or customers’ history—which allows for personalized treatment. We focus on consistency (vanishing regret compared with optimal policy) and show that for large classes of non-independent and identically distributed (non-i.i.d.) contexts, consistency can be achieved regardless of the reward mechanism, a property known as universal consistency. papers.title: ZipAEr: A compressive convolutional autoencoder for high-dimensional spatial omics data at subcellular resolution
papers.summary: Background Recent advances in spatial transcriptomics, such as the CosMx Spatial Molecular Imager, enable the detection and quantification of thousands of RNA transcripts at subcellular resolution. While these data offer unprecedented insight, computational analysis remains a significant bottleneck. Current methods typically aggregate transcripts at the cell level, relying on precise cell segmentation—a notoriously difficult task in complex tissues like the brain. papers.title: Embodied Strings: A Biosensing-Based VR Guqin for Spatial Musical Expression
papers.summary: Motivation• Gugin performance is an embodied musical practice where bodily motion shapes sonic expression.Yet, remaining hard to convey via notation or screen-based interfaces.• Existing digital Guqin systems focus on gesture recognition or pedagogy, overlooking the muscular effort behind musical expression.• Biosensor technologies (e.g., electromyography (EMG)) can capture the muscle activity, opening new ways of making music.

papers.title: British Art Studies
papers.summary: In this conversation, Noski Deville and Nicola Singh reflect on their recent collaboration to craft a contemporary response to Deville’s film Loss of Heat (1994). They describe their working processes and how they created new artworks that respond to the restoration, preservation, and screening of Loss of Heat by Cinenova in 2022. With their interviewer, Beth Bramich, they discuss embodied aspects of film and intergenerational collaboration, and explore the possibilities of combining film with sound art, written and spoken text, and live performance. papers.title: Unsupervised reward-driven image segmentation in automated scanning transmission electron microscopy experiments
papers.summary: Automated experiments in scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) require rapid image segmentation to optimize the data representation for human interpretation, decision-making, site-selective spectroscopy, and atomic manipulation. Currently, segmentation tasks are typically performed using supervised machine learning methods, which require human-labeled data and are sensitive to out-of-distribution drift effects caused by changes in resolution, sampling, or beam shape. papers.title: Sculpting ultrafast mid-infrared light for solid-state high-harmonic generation
papers.summary: The ability to sculpt light in space, time, and polarization has revolutionized studies of light–matter interaction and enabled breakthroughs in optical communication, imaging, and ultrafast science. Among the many degrees of freedom of light, orbital angular momentum (OAM) further expands these capabilities by unlocking new regimes of control in information encoding, particle trapping and manipulation, and symmetry-driven selection rules. papers.title: Optical detection and manipulation of pseudospin orders in Wigner crystals
papers.summary: In Wigner-crystal states of two-dimensional electrons, the spin ordering remains poorly understood. The small energy differences between candidate spin orders make theoretical studies less reliable, and probing magnetic order at a nonzero wave vector is experimentally challenging. In modern realizations of Wigner crystals, the electronic spin degree of freedom is often replaced by a valley pseudospin associated with nonzero Berry curvature. papers.title: Generating persistent-current superpositions in Bose-Einstein condensates using dynamic optical potentials
papers.summary: Precise and flexible manipulation of the motional state of ultracold atoms is a fundamental enabling technology for diverse applications such as quantum sensing and quantum computation. In this paper, we propose a general, simple, and highly efficient method to engineer the motional state of a Bose-Einstein condensate with time-dependent optical fields, which can be realized experimentally with existing light sculpting techniques. papers.title: Well-posedness and instability of free electron quantum tomography
papers.summary: Recent advancements in photon induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM) enable the preparation, coherent manipulation and characterization of free-electron quantum states. The available measurement consists of electron energy spectrograms and the goal is the reconstruction of a density matrix representing the quantum state. This requires the solution of a constrained linear inverse problem, where a positive semi-definite trace-class operator is reconstructed given its diagonal in different bases. papers.title: Measuring ESG risk in supply networks
papers.summary: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) rating is a way for investors to prioritize investments in companies with good corporate behavior. However, ESG ratings are vulnerable to manipulation in a number of ways. In this paper we study how trade with badly rated companies can affect a target company’s own rating. To do this, we introduce a scoring framework to account for the effect of bad actors deep in the supply chain. papers.title: Task Framing Effects on Personality-Based Team Formation
papers.summary: This study examines how task framing influences personality-based team selection decisions. Participants will form four-person teams for an entrepreneurial venture after reading task descriptions that vary in their emphasis on different work approaches. We will analyze whether framing systematically shifts which personality traits people prioritize when selecting teammates, and whether this produces differences in team diversity. papers.title: Directional scattering induced optical forces on a Mie particle near a metal interface
papers.summary: Optical manipulation of Mie-resonant dielectric nanoparticles is strongly influenced by their enhanced scattering and multipolar response, which fundamentally modify the balance of optical forces. In this work, we study the optical forces acting on a resonant dielectric nanoparticle placed near a metal interface, where scattering occurs into both free-space and surface plasmon-polariton (SPP) channels.
